title: Calibration artifact promotion & multi-tenant SLAs
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Design and implement a staged artifact promotion workflow for calibration runs that supports multi-tenant isolation and tenant-level SLAs. The goal is to make calibration outputs (quant profiles, statistics, calibration logs) promotable from ephemeral candidate runs to signed, immutable 'stable' artifacts that downstream serving and optimize pipelines can depend on. This includes retention/TTL policies, legal-hold paths, and role-based approval gates for promotion and deletion.
background: Current calibration runs produce artifacts in a shared bucket with coarse TTLs and no clear promotion path. Customers running Dedicated and Private deployments need: (1) repeatable artifact provenance, (2) per-tenant retention/GC rules, (3) audit trail for promotions and rollbacks, and (4) SLA guarantees for availability of 'stable' quant profiles used in production.
goals: Define promotion lifecycle: candidate -> validated -> stable -> archived
Per-tenant retention and legal-hold controls with sensible defaults
Composable RBAC around calibration runs and artifact promotions
Automated accuracy validation gating against golden prompt sets
Provide UI affordances in Console for promotion, revoke, and artifact lineage
out_of_scope: Full encryption/HSM integration (handled by KMS project)
On-prem air-gapped transfer mechanics (covered by Private deployment task)
Low-level kernel runtime changes for quantization accuracy
success_metrics: % of production services using a 'stable' artifact increases to 90% within 3 weeks of rollout
Mean time to find a validated artifact for a tenant < 2 minutes
Incidents due to stale/unverified quant profiles reduced by 95%
Audit events emitted for every promotion/deletion with user identity
acceptance_criteria: Console: UI flow to promote a candidate run to 'validated' with a one-click accuracy check against tenant golden set
Backend: artifact metadata stores immutable provenance fields (run_id, model_version, dataset_snapshot_id, checksums, signer)
RBAC: new roles CalibrationRunner and ArtifactApprover with configurable scopes per-organization and per-project
Retention: per-tenant policy applied at creation and enforced by GC service, and legal-hold prevents deletion
APIs: promotion and revoke endpoints with audit logs and idempotent semantics
CI: automated accuracy regression test that trips a canary failure if stable artifact deviates beyond threshold
technical_notes: Artifact store model: append-only object store + metadata catalog (per-tenant namespace)
Promotion implemented as metadata mutation (set state) and cryptographic signature by Approver service
Dataset snapshot: create read-only snapshot references for evaluation to preserve reproducibility
Accuracy validation: run evaluation harness in isolated job against golden prompt set; use diff-metrics (token-level BLEU-like + model-specific scoring)
GC: two-phase GC — candidate TTL short (default 7d), validated TTL medium (30d), stable TTL long (90d), configurable per-tenant
Cost trade-off: keeping stable artifacts long increases storage; propose tiered storage lifecycle to S3 Glacier-equivalent for archived artifacts
rollout_plan: Week 1: Backend metadata catalog + RBAC hooks (ENG: core-storage, infra)
Week 2: Console UI for promotion and lineage viewer; integrate evaluation harness (QA + PM review)
Week 3: Tenant pilot with three customers (one Hosted, one Dedicated, one Private); collect feedback and tune TTLs
Week 4: Roll out defaults and enable opt-in tenant policies; ship console-2025.04 release
risks: Cross-tenant leakage if namespace isolation not enforced — mitigated by per-tenant catalog and encryption keys
Promoting a candidate with insufficient eval coverage could regress production — mitigated by mandatory accuracy checks for promotion to 'validated' for tenants with production flag
Storage costs could rise significantly if many tenants pin stable artifacts — mitigated by tiered lifecycle and soft-quota alerts
Approval bottleneck: manual ArtifactApprover role could become a release blocker — mitigate via automation and SLOs for approval turnaround
open_questions: Should promotion require a human approver for all tenants, or only for tenants with production=true?
What are default TTL values for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tenants?
Do we allow cross-tenant artifact sharing with explicit grant, or restrict to same-organization only?
How to surface accuracy delta significance (statistical vs practical) in Console to assist approvers?
